title: FRIA vs DPIA: two assessments, one workflow
linkedinPost:
Most regulated banks in Europe have a DPIA process. Almost none have started their FRIA. The 2 August 2026 deadline under EU AI Act Article 27 is 25 days away.

Here's the difference that matters:

The DPIA asks: what personal data are you processing and what are the risks to data subjects?

The FRIA asks: who is affected by your AI system's decisions — and could those decisions discriminate, deny access to finance, or block a meaningful remedy?

A credit scoring model can produce proxy discrimination without ever processing a protected characteristic. The DPIA won't catch it. The FRIA must.

What I would do if I were COO at a regulated European institution right now:

• Audit every AI system against EU AI Act Annex III — credit scoring, insurance risk, employment, recruitment
• Build a combined FRIA/DPIA template: the FRIA is Layer 2 on top of your existing DPIA structure, not a separate document
• Register each AI system in a live governance system — deadline, deployer, FRIA status, open mitigations
• Don't wait for the official EU AI Office template — it hadn't been published as of June 2026

The cost of manual FRIA documentation: 30–50 hours per AI system at blended legal rates. With 8+ AI systems in scope, that's 240–400 hours of compliance work. Revenue per employee problem hiding in plain sight.

Full piece + the Dual-Layer Compliance Protocol I built around this — link in comments.

mainEntity.name: Is a FRIA the same as a DPIA?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. A DPIA assesses risks to data subjects from personal data processing under GDPR Article 35. A FRIA assesses risks to all EU Charter fundamental rights from high-risk AI deployment under EU AI Act Article 27. They have different legal bases, different scopes, and different obligation holders. Where both apply, run them as integrated sequential layers of one document.

mainEntity.name: When does the FRIA obligation apply to financial services?

acceptedAnswer.text: FRIA requirements under Article 27 apply to deployers of Annex III high-risk AI systems — primarily credit scoring, insurance risk pricing, employment management, and recruitment AI. The original 2 August 2026 deadline applies to certain categories; a June 2026 EU Parliament amendment extended some Annex III timelines to December 2027. Verify your specific use case against the updated schedule.

mainEntity.name: What if I've already done a DPIA — do I still need a FRIA?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The DPIA discharges the GDPR obligation; it does not discharge the AI Act obligation. Article 27(4) states that the FRIA should complement an existing DPIA where they overlap, but it is a separate legal requirement with its own fine exposure — up to €15M or 3% of global annual turnover.

mainEntity.name: What if the EU AI Office template hasn't been published yet?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of June 2026, the official questionnaire required by Article 27(5) had not been released by the European AI Office. The obligation still applies. Use independently developed templates structured around Article 27's required elements. When the official template is published, review and update your documentation for alignment.
